title: HashMap essentials
summary: insert and get for single keys; entry().or_insert() for update-or-create.
lecture: `HashMap<K, V>` stores values by key. `insert` writes, `get` returns an `Option` because the key may be absent. Indexing with `map[key]` panics on a missing key - fine for known keys, wrong for counting.
The counting idiom is `entry`: `map.entry(key).or_insert(0)` returns a mutable reference to the existing value, inserting the default first if needed. Bump it through the reference: `*count += 1`.
That `*` matters: the entry API hands you a `&mut i32`, and `+=` works on the value, not the reference (E0368 if you forget).

example.caption: One line handles both the first and every later sighting.
